documents.title: Guidance on the Use of AI in Teaching and Learning
tiers: Option 2: Limited or Guided AI Use
Option 3: AI Use Encouraged with Transparency
documents.summary: NIU university guidance that leaves AI rules to faculty and offers three sample syllabus frameworks. It adds principles, definitions, disclosure and assessment advice, a data-upload limit and support resources.
documents.stance_why: The page says "faculty have primary responsibility for determining whether and how AI tools may be used" and offers three sample frameworks ("Faculty should include one of the following"), so the university sets no rule itself.

units.why: The purpose list says the guidance will "provide flexibility for faculty to determine appropriate use", which places the decision with each instructor, so it is a stance-and-who-decides rule (P04).
units.anchor: Provide flexibility for faculty to determine appropriate use within their courses.

units.why: "Align AI use with existing NIU policies on academic integrity, data privacy and intellectual property" requires AI use to follow existing university policy, which is P77; P45 does not fit because no collaborator analogy is drawn.
units.anchor: Align AI use with existing NIU policies on academic integrity, data privacy and intellectual property

units.why: "This guidance does not replace existing university policies" states the guidance's scope and status as shared language, an institution-level framework statement (P56).
units.anchor: This guidance does not replace existing university policies
units.policy: The guidance does not replace existing university policies and offers instructional support and shared language that faculty may adapt for their courses.

units.why: "Decisions about AI use should be driven by learning outcomes, not the availability of tools" is a guiding principle for how AI decisions are made; it is a framework principle (P56) rather than a skill-building warning (P41).
units.anchor: Decisions about AI use should be driven by learning outcomes, not the availability of tools.

units.why: "Expectations for AI use should be clearly communicated to students in syllabi, assignments and course materials" asks that AI expectations be stated in syllabi and assignments, which is P09.
units.anchor: clearly communicated to students in syllabi, assignments and course materials.

units.why: "Faculty should consider student access, cost, accessibility and potential bias" addresses equity and bias when integrating AI; P51 is closest, but it also names bias and only asks faculty to consider, not to provide alternatives.
units.anchor: Faculty should consider student access, cost, accessibility and potential bias when integrating AI tools.
units.fit_note: Also names bias as a consideration and only asks faculty to consider these factors; it does not require free access or alternatives.

units.why: "AI use must align with NIU's academic integrity expectations, including proper attribution and disclosure when required" makes attribution and disclosure a duty when required, which is P24.
units.anchor: including proper attribution and disclosure when required
units.fit_note: Also ties AI use to academic integrity expectations generally.

units.why: "AI tools should support-rather than replace-critical thinking, creativity and disciplinary learning" keeps the student as the thinker and rules out AI replacing thinking (P32).
units.anchor: AI tools should support—rather than replace—critical thinking, creativity and disciplinary learning.

units.why: This defines "artificial intelligence (AI)" for the guidance, which sets what the guidance covers (P61).
units.anchor: refers to computer systems (including software programs, websites and apps)
units.policy: For instructional purposes, artificial intelligence (AI) refers to computer systems (including software programs, websites and apps) that can perform tasks typically associated with human intelligence, such as analyzing data, recognizing patterns or generating content.

units.why: "Generative AI tools can create new text, images, audio, video or code" defines generative AI and so sets the scope (P61).
units.anchor: tools can create new text, images, audio, video or code in response to user prompts.

units.why: Student conduct and tool use, "including emerging technologies such as AI", are "guided by NIU's existing academic policies", so AI use falls under existing policies (P77), not a new AI-specific rule.
units.anchor: guided by NIU's existing academic policies

units.why: "NIU is actively reviewing and updating guidance to make expectations related to AI use more explicit" says the guidance is provisional and will change (P54).
units.anchor: NIU is actively reviewing and updating guidance to make expectations related to AI use

units.why: "Faculty have primary responsibility for determining whether and how AI tools may be used in their courses" puts the decision with instructors, which is P04.
units.anchor: primary responsibility for determining whether and how AI tools may be used in their courses

units.why: The list "Discipline / Course level / Learning objectives / Type of assignment" says acceptable use varies by context; this is per-course and per-assignment variation of the rule (P04).
units.anchor: Acceptable use may vary by
units.policy: Acceptable use of AI may vary by discipline, course level (undergraduate vs. graduate), learning objectives, and type of assignment or assessment.

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to make expectations explicit rather than assuming a single, institution-wide rule" asks instructors to state their own AI rule, which is P09; it also rejects a single university rule.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to make expectations explicit rather than assuming a single, institution-wide rule.

units.why: "Faculty should include one of the following policy approaches in their syllabus or assignment instructions" requires a syllabus AI statement, which is P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should include one of the following policy approaches in their syllabus or assignment instructions.

units.why: The three sample frameworks (not permitted / limited or guided / encouraged with transparency) are named levels of AI use for faculty to adopt, which is P05.
units.anchor: Option 1: AI Use Not Permitted
units.policy: NIU offers three sample course policy frameworks: Option 1 AI Use Not Permitted, Option 2 Limited or Guided AI Use, Option 3 AI Use Encouraged with Transparency.

units.why: Option 1 says students "may not use generative AI tools to complete course assignments unless explicitly authorized", a default ban with permission as the exception (P01).
units.anchor: Students may not use generative AI tools to complete course assignments unless explicitly authorized.
units.fit_note: This is a sample option for faculty to adopt, not a rule that binds all NIU students.

units.why: "Use of AI-generated content without permission may be considered a violation of academic integrity" classifies unauthorized use as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Use of AI-generated content without permission may be considered a violation of academic integrity.

units.why: Option 2 allows AI "for specific purposes (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, editing for clarity)", a narrow list of permitted uses; P15 fits brainstorming but outlining and editing also appear, so I note the fit.
units.anchor: Students may use AI tools for specific purposes (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, editing for clarity)
units.policy: Students may use AI tools for specific purposes (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, editing for clarity) as outlined in the assignment instructions.
units.fit_note: Also lists outlining and editing for clarity, and ties the allowed purposes to each assignment's instructions.

units.why: "Use beyond these purposes is not permitted" bans anything outside the listed purposes, a limit on the narrow list; P01 is the nearest default-ban type.
units.anchor: Use beyond these purposes is not permitted
units.fit_note: Applies only to uses outside the narrow list in Option 2; it is not a blanket ban.

units.why: "and must be disclosed when required" makes disclosure a condition of AI use under Option 2, which is P24.
units.anchor: must be disclosed when required

units.why: Option 3 says "Students are encouraged to use AI tools as part of the learning process", which welcomes AI by default (P02).
units.anchor: Students are encouraged to use AI tools as part of the learning process.

units.why: Option 3 requires students to "document how they were used and reflect on their impact on learning", i.e. keep and submit documentation and reflections (P26).
units.anchor: students must document how they were used and reflect on their impact on learning

units.why: Faculty "are encouraged to specify" tools, disclosure and evaluation, which asks instructors to state concrete expectations (P09).
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to specify:
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged to specify what tools are allowed or discouraged, what disclosure is required, and how student work will be evaluated.

units.why: "faculty may require students to: Acknowledge the use of AI tools" lets instructors require acknowledgement of AI use, which is P24.
units.anchor: faculty may require students to:
units.frag_start: When AI use is permitted, faculty may
units.frag_end: Acknowledge the use of AI tools
units.policy: When AI use is permitted, faculty may require students to acknowledge the use of AI tools.

units.why: "Describe how the tool was used (e.g., brainstorming, drafting, revising)" asks for detail on how AI was used; P25 is about tool, prompt and output details, so I assign it with a note.
units.anchor: Describe how the tool was used (e.g., brainstorming, drafting, revising)
units.policy: When AI use is permitted, faculty may require students to describe how the tool was used (e.g., brainstorming, drafting, revising).
units.fit_note: Asks for a description of the kind of use, not the tool name, prompt or output.

units.why: "Retain responsibility for the accuracy, originality and integrity of submitted work" makes students answerable for what they submit (P29).
units.anchor: Retain responsibility for the accuracy, originality and integrity of submitted work
units.policy: When AI use is permitted, faculty may require students to retain responsibility for the accuracy, originality and integrity of submitted work.

units.why: "Students remain accountable for meeting course learning outcomes, regardless of AI assistance" keeps students responsible for outcomes whatever AI does (P29).
units.anchor: Students remain accountable for meeting course learning outcomes, regardless of AI assistance.

units.why: "Emphasizing process, reflection and iteration" recommends redesigning assessment around process rather than product because of AI (P35).
units.anchor: Emphasizing process, reflection and iteration
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged to reflect on how AI tools may affect assessment design, including emphasizing process, reflection and iteration.

units.why: "Incorporating in-class, oral or applied assessments" moves assessment toward in-class and oral formats; P33 (proctored, unassisted) is closest and P34 (oral checks) also touches it, but the item is about assessment format, so P33 with a note.
units.anchor: Incorporating in-class, oral or applied assessments
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged to reflect on how AI tools may affect assessment design, including incorporating in-class, oral or applied assessments.
units.fit_note: Also names oral and applied assessments (P34-like); does not say assessments are proctored or unassisted.

units.why: "Designing assignments that require discipline-specific judgment or personal context" redesigns assignments around AI limits (P35).
units.anchor: Designing assignments that require discipline-specific judgment or personal context
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged to reflect on how AI tools may affect assessment design, including designing assignments that require discipline-specific judgment or personal context.

units.why: Learning activities where students "critically examine and evaluate AI outputs... rather than simply prohibiting AI use" redesign coursework around AI and discourage bans; P35 fits the activity design and the note records the anti-ban stance.
units.anchor: rather than simply prohibiting AI use
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged to create learning activities where students critically examine and evaluate AI outputs, limitations and impacts, rather than simply prohibiting AI use.
units.fit_note: Also states a preference for critical engagement over simple prohibition and asks students to evaluate AI output.

units.why: "many AI tools collect and store user data... may use submitted content for training" is a privacy fact that grounds the data rule (P50).
units.anchor: Faculty and students should be mindful that many AI tools:
units.frag_start: Faculty and students should be mindful
units.policy: Faculty and students should be mindful that many AI tools collect and store user data, may use submitted content for training purposes, and are subject to vendor terms of service outside NIU control.

units.why: "Do not upload student work, grades or non-public instructional materials into public AI tools unless the tool has been institutionally approved" bans uploading protected materials; P49 fits, with a note that it binds faculty too and permits approved tools.
units.anchor: Do not upload student work, grades or non-public instructional materials into public AI tools
units.fit_note: Addressed to faculty and students alike and covers student work and grades; allows institutionally approved tools.

units.why: AI use in research "must align with NIU's Research Misconduct Policy" governs AI in scholarship by deferring to existing policy (P62).
units.anchor: their use must align with NIU's
units.frag_start: When AI tools are used in research
units.policy: When AI tools are used in research or scholarly activity, their use must align with NIU's Research Misconduct Policy.

units.why: "AI tools should not be used in ways that undermine research integrity or ethical standards" is a research-conduct limit (P62).
units.anchor: AI tools should not be used in ways that undermine research integrity or ethical standards.
units.frag_start: AI tools should not be used

units.why: The CITL, "faculty development workshops and consultations" are support for instructors learning about AI, which is P63.
units.anchor: Faculty development workshops and consultations
units.policy: NIU provides faculty development workshops and consultations, through the Center for Innovative Teaching and Learning, on AI.

units.why: "Academic integrity tutorials for students and faculty" and "Student-facing AI literacy resources" are AI training offered to students and staff (P70).
units.anchor: Student-facing AI literacy resources
units.policy: NIU provides academic integrity tutorials for students and faculty and student-facing AI literacy resources.

units.why: "Library-supported guidance on research, citation and academic integrity" points students to library staff as human help (P72).
units.anchor: Library-supported guidance on research, citation and academic integrity
units.policy: NIU provides library-supported guidance on research, citation and academic integrity.
units.fit_note: Presented as a general support service; not specifically tied to AI use.

units.why: "Additional training and resources will continue to be developed as AI technologies evolve" commits to growing AI training over time (P70; P54 would fit only the policy-review sense).
units.anchor: Additional training and resources will continue to be developed as AI technologies evolve.

documents.title: AI guidance for students
documents.summary: Student guidance hub listing licensed AI tools, training and an FAQ. It tells students to follow the syllabus, ask the professor when unsure, disclose AI use, and not pass off AI work as their own.
documents.stance_why: Student-facing page: "Your professor determines if and how AI technologies may be used in coursework" and "It depends on your course", so the decision sits with instructors.

units.why: "promoting responsible and innovative uses of AI in learning" and building "skills needed to apply AI thoughtfully" frames AI skills as something NIU aims to teach, which is P44.
units.anchor: NIU helps students build the knowledge and skills needed to apply AI thoughtfully across disciplines.

units.why: "Faculty and staff are encouraged to stay informed about their responsibilities related to protecting the security and privacy of personal data" asks employees to protect data when using AI (P50).
units.anchor: protecting the security and privacy of personal data and intellectual property when using AI tools

units.why: "NIU provides a number of approved AI tools" covered by vendor agreements; this is the university providing sanctioned tools (P17).
units.anchor: NIU provides a number of approved AI tools and technologies to support teaching and learning.
units.frag_start: NIU provides a number of approved

units.why: "NIU recommends that students, faculty and staff use only AI tools that have been vetted and approved" recommends vetted tools, which is P50.
units.anchor: students, faculty and staff use only AI tools that have been vetted and approved

units.why: Adobe Firefly, Express and Creative Cloud are listed as licensed tools "available to all NIU faculty" and for students, a university-provided AI tool (P17).
units.anchor: Use AI-powered features like image generation in Adobe Firefly and Express

units.why: Microsoft 365 Copilot is offered with "commercial data protection to safeguard sensitive university data", a licensed assistant with data protection (P17).
units.anchor: NIU’s M365 license includes commercial data protection to safeguard sensitive university data

units.why: Quinncia is a licensed AI tool that gives "personalized feedback on their resume, LinkedIn profile and interview skills", offered to NIU students (P17).
units.anchor: AI to give students personalized feedback on their resume, LinkedIn profile and interview skills

units.why: The Training list ("AI and Academic Integrity Tutorial", "AI in Education Tutorial") shows NIU offers AI training to the community (P70).
units.anchor: AI and Academic Integrity Tutorial
units.policy: NIU offers an AI and Academic Integrity Tutorial, an AI Tools for Research Workshop Recording and an AI in Education Tutorial.

units.why: "Your professor determines if and how AI technologies may be used in coursework" gives the decision to the instructor, which is P04.
units.anchor: Your professor determines if and how AI technologies may be used in coursework.

units.why: "If you're not sure, check your syllabus and/or ask before using AI" tells unsure students to ask first (P10).
units.anchor: If you’re not sure, check your syllabus and/or ask before using AI.

units.why: "Start with the syllabus and assignment instructions. If the course policy is unclear, contact your professor for guidance before using AI" is guidance on where to find the rule and to ask when unclear (P10).
units.anchor: If the course policy is unclear, contact your professor for guidance before using AI.

units.why: "Many faculty will require acknowledgement and/or citation when AI meaningfully contributes" informs students that disclosure is often required (P24).
units.anchor: Many faculty will require acknowledgement and/or citation when AI meaningfully contributes

units.why: "examples of course AI policies (ranging from prohibited, to permitted with permission, to permitted with acknowledgement)" describes a range of levels of use (P05).
units.anchor: ranging from prohibited, to permitted with permission, to permitted with acknowledgement

units.why: "Disclosure is always preferable to silence" tells students to disclose; it also treats disclosure as safer, so P24 with a note.
units.anchor: Disclosure is always preferable to silence.
units.fit_note: Also frames disclosure as the safer choice over saying nothing.

units.why: "be transparent about how you used it... and follow your professor's specific instructions for acknowledgement or citation" asks students to describe use; P25 with a note since no tool/prompt details are named.
units.anchor: be transparent about how you used it
units.frag_start: If you used AI in any meaningful way,
units.policy: If you used AI in any meaningful way, be transparent about how you used it (for example, brainstorming ideas, outlining, checking clarity or revising language) and follow your professor's specific instructions for acknowledgement or citation.
units.fit_note: Asks for a description of how AI was used, not the tool, prompt or output; defers format to the professor.

units.why: "Clear, proactive disclosure helps protect you from misunderstandings and potential academic integrity concerns" says disclosure lowers integrity risk, which is P28.
units.anchor: Clear, proactive disclosure helps protect you from misunderstandings and potential academic integrity
units.fit_note: Says disclosure protects students but does not promise disclosed use is never penalized.

units.why: "always review your syllabus and assignment guidelines and ask your professor if you are unsure how AI use should be disclosed" is an ask-first rule on disclosure (P10).
units.anchor: ask your professor if you are unsure how AI use should be disclosed

units.why: "Don't submit AI-generated work as if it's solely your own if your professor doesn't allow it" bans passing off AI output as one's own where not allowed (P19).
units.anchor: Don't submit AI-generated work as if it's solely your own if your professor
units.frag_start: Don't submit AI-generated work as if
units.fit_note: Conditional on the professor's rule and on disclosure; covers all AI-generated work, not only code.

units.why: "academic dishonesty applies broadly in the academic environment" and links AI misuse to academic dishonesty and research misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: applies broadly in the academic environment

units.why: "Submitting AI-generated text that closely mirrors existing books, articles or websites" names a plagiarism risk; it is a misconduct example (P36).
units.anchor: Submitting AI-generated text that closely mirrors existing books, articles or websites
units.frag_start: Submitting AI-generated text that closely mirrors
units.fit_note: Gives a specific example (text mirroring existing sources) of AI-related plagiarism.

units.why: "Copying or lightly editing AI output that reproduces ideas or language from a real author without a citation" is named as plagiarism and misattribution (P36).
units.anchor: AI output that reproduces ideas or language from a real author without a citation
units.frag_start: Copying or lightly editing AI output
units.fit_note: Example of misattribution; concerns citing real authors rather than disclosing AI.

units.why: "Relying on AI-generated citations without checking the original sources" is warned against because AI citations can be wrong; this is P31.
units.anchor: Relying on AI-generated citations without checking the original sources

units.why: "Citing sources you have not personally read or verified" is named as a misattribution risk that requires students to verify (P31).
units.anchor: Citing sources you have not personally read or verified

units.why: "Read the original sources yourself" tells students to check what AI points to (P31).
units.anchor: Read the original sources yourself

units.why: "Write in your own words and academic voice" requires the submitted writing to be the student's own (P29).
units.anchor: Write in your own words and academic voice

units.why: "Cite real authors and publications accurately" is a citation-accuracy duty for work with AI; P31 fits best since it guards against fabricated references.
units.anchor: Cite real authors and publications accurately
units.fit_note: Concerns citing real sources accurately, not verifying AI output in general.

units.why: "Disclose permitted AI use when required by your professor" is a disclosure duty (P24).
units.anchor: Disclose permitted AI use when required by your professor

units.why: "Become familiar with NIU's Student Code of Conduct and course-specific AI policies" points students to existing conduct rules (P77).
units.anchor: Become familiar with NIU’s
units.policy: Students should become familiar with NIU's Student Code of Conduct and course-specific AI policies and ask their professor if unsure whether a particular use of AI is allowed or how it should be acknowledged.
units.fit_note: Also tells students to ask the professor when unsure (P10).

units.why: "How you decide to engage with AI should be guided by these values" ties AI use to the Northern Pact, an institution-level value statement (P56).
units.anchor: How you decide to engage with AI should be guided by these values.

units.why: "If you rely on AI, you miss out on the benefits of learning which involves your own thinking" gives the reason: AI shortcuts the practice that builds skill (P41).
units.anchor: If you rely on AI, you miss out on the benefits of learning

units.why: "Using AI eliminates the necessary friction to learn" is another statement that AI removes productive struggle (P41).
units.anchor: Using AI eliminates the necessary friction to learn.

units.why: "using AI simply to obtain answers also carries a real environmental cost" names an environmental harm of AI (P53).
units.anchor: using AI simply to obtain answers also carries a real environmental cost

units.why: "it's worth weighing whether the educational benefit justifies the environmental impact" asks students to weigh environmental cost before using AI (P53).
units.anchor: worth weighing whether the educational benefit justifies the environmental impact involved
units.frag_start: When AI use is not necessary for learning,

units.why: The AI Ethical Guidelines are described as "values and practices to guide responsible, equitable, and transparent use of AI" at NIU, a framework for principles (P56).
units.anchor: Concise set of values and practices to guide responsible, equitable, and transparent use of AI

units.why: The Student Guide and AI Literacies Framework are AI-literacy resources for students ("use them responsibly and critically as part of their learning and future careers") (P70).
units.anchor: how to use them responsibly and critically as part of their learning and future careers
units.frag_start: The Student Guide to Artificial Intelligence

notes: No school or computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred (collect file). Two documents only. The students page links to AI Ethical Guidelines, Literacies Framework and Student Guide but only their link descriptions are in the saved text.
